definition: Tracing and Observability is a core concept in Agentic AI. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Tracing and Observability is
theory.body: Tracing and Observability describes the methods and patterns used within Agentic AI to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Tracing and Observability is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Tracing and Observability matters
theory.body: Without Tracing and Observability, systems built with Agentic AI are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Tracing and Observability works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Tracing and Observability follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Tracing and Observability.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Tracing and Observability
theory.body: Tracing and Observability offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
